review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the sibling file `..._exists_dTot_eq_single_augTot_sub_single_augCech_cup.lean`, which repeats these helper declarations and uses `ent`, `map_aval` and `aval_val`. I did not run Lean. The file has no @[simp] attributes and very little simp use, so the findings are about missing simp-facing equation lemmas and missing canonical rewrite attributes. Both are judgement calls: I have not tested that the proposed lemmas fire under simp, and `aval`'s dependent proof argument could make simp matching harder in some uses.

findings.excerpt: if hA : r + pq.1.1 + 1 = p ∧ pq.1.2 = q then
findings.problem: `ent` is a branching definition (dite with two guards, else 0) that is exposed with no equation lemmas. The only way to evaluate it is `unfold ent; dsimp only; rw [dif_pos/dif_neg ...]`, followed by a `show` to restate the unfolded body. The sibling file repeats this pattern in `res_ent_A`, `res_ent_B` and `res_ent_zero`. The three cases are therefore reproved by hand and simp cannot normalise `ent … ⟨(a,b),hab⟩ (s,t)` once the guards are known. The `omit K s t in` / `show Γ(…) from` casts also make unfolding fragile.
findings.proposed_change: Add three conditional equation lemmas right after the definition: `ent_of_A` (hypothesis `r + a + 1 = p ∧ b = q`, RHS the `(-1)^r • (aval … * aval …)` term), `ent_of_B` (hypothesis `p ≤ r ∧ a = 0 ∧ r + b + 1 = p + q`, together with `¬` of the A-guard), and `ent_zero` (both guards false, RHS `0`). Tag them `@[simp]` or use them with `simp [ent_of_A hA]`. This lets simp discharge the side conditions by `omega`/`simp` and removes `unfold ent; dsimp only; rw [dif_pos …]` from the consumers.
findings.benefit: Every use of `ent` can rewrite by a named lemma instead of unfolding a dite. The case guards are discharged as side conditions, and downstream proofs such as `res_ent_A`/`res_ent_B`/`res_ent_zero` shrink to one `rw` or `simp` call each.

evidence.excerpt:
unfold ent
  dsimp only
  rw [dif_pos (show r + a + 1 = p ∧ b = q from ⟨hA, hq⟩)]

findings.excerpt: theorem map_aval (u : Fin (p + 1) → 𝔘.ι) {O O' : P.Opens} (h : O ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝔘.ointer u) (i : O' ≤ O) :
findings.problem: `map_aval` is the canonical restriction-compatibility rewrite for `aval`. It has a clear direction, since the LHS is a restriction of an `aval` and the RHS is a single `aval` on the smaller open. Its proof-term argument `i.trans h` is a Prop, so it does not block rewriting. It is not tagged for simp, so the main proof chains it by hand (`map_aval` four times, plus `unitPullback_eq_aval` twice). The sibling file repeats this and also lists it after `map_zsmul, map_mul` in a hand-ordered `rw`. `aval_congr` and `aval_val` are not marked either. A user who unfolds a `res` of a product of avals cannot simply call `simp`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `map_aval` as `@[simp]`. Optionally also mark `unitPullback_eq_aval` as `@[simp]`, since it rewrites `unitPullback … s` to the `aval` normal form. Replace the line `rw [unitPullback_eq_aval, unitPullback_eq_aval, map_aval, map_aval, map_aval, map_aval, OModulePresheaf.unit_smul]` with a `simp only [unitPullback_eq_aval, map_aval, OModulePresheaf.unit_smul]` or a plain `simp` call. In `res_cup` and `res_ent_*` the same change removes the repeated `map_aval, map_aval, map_aval` sequences.
findings.benefit: The normal form (`aval` on the smallest open) is stated once and reached by simp. Proofs no longer depend on counting how many `map_aval` rewrites are needed, and they no longer break when the number of factors changes.

evidence.excerpt: rw [unitPullback_eq_aval, unitPullback_eq_aval, map_aval, map_aval, map_aval, map_aval, OModulePresheaf.unit_smul]
